blocks.title: Short-hand if-else
blocks.text: Python allows an if-else to be written on one line: action_if_true if condition else action_if_false.

blocks.title: Python code (each .... is one 4-space indent)
blocks.text:
temperature = 15
print("It's a hot day") if temperature > 30 else print("It's not a hot day")
This does the same as the previous example in a more compact form: it prints "It's a hot day" if temperature is greater than 30, otherwise "It's not a hot day".

blocks.prompt: How does the short-hand if-else differ from the regular if-else (short question 4)?
blocks.explanation: It puts the whole choice on one line and gives one value or action for each case, which suits simple choices; the regular if-else uses separate indented blocks and can hold several statements in each branch.

items: Short hand: x if condition else y on one line; same result as a two-branch if-else.
